newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: The Spanish debt market held on to gains by Tuesday's close but vertigo put a cap on prices which set records earlier in the session.
"The market is strong but this latest rally needs same consolidation in the short run," a Madrid-based dealer said.
April CPI, to be announced on Wednesday morning, is expected to fall to an historic 30-year low, up 1.9 percent year-on-year versus 2.2 percent in March.
Dealers said any further decline in the inflation rate would prompt the Bank of Spain to ease its key money market rate again as early as Friday.
"If tomorrow's CPI is in line with forecast, I'd say the market will take profits after that," another dealer said.
He stressed that after such strong gains, profit-taking was normal, especially one day before a public holiday. On Thursday, the market is expected to be closed for a public holiday in Madrid.
The 10-year yield spread over Bunds hit a record low in the morning at 83 basis points. It ended at 85 basis points.
